title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 16
paragraphs: The Chians, with the remainder of their ships, fled away to their own land; but those of the Chians whose ships had been disabled by the damage they had received, being pursued, fled for refuge to Mycale; there they ran their ships ashore, left them behind, and proceeded on foot over the mainland. When the Chians had entered the territory of Ephesus on their way—coming into it by night, just at a time when a festival of the Thesmophoria was being celebrated by the women of the place—the Ephesians, not having heard beforehand how matters stood with the Chians and seeing an armed body entering their land, assumed for certain that they were robbers with a design on the women; so they came out in a body to the rescue and killed the Chians.
